user: Fine. Back to that charge — what do I do next?
answer:
What I did
- Reviewed the dispute rules and the prior eligibility check you mentioned.

What I found
- The “goods not received” reason is governed by a 90‑day dispute window from the transaction date.
- If we open a dispute you may be asked for supporting evidence (order confirmation, delivery tracking or proof of attempted delivery, and any correspondence with the merchant). If evidence is requested you must supply it within 7 calendar days or the case may be declined.
- You already have a formal eligibility check saying this transaction is eligible to be disputed.

What you can do next (choose one)
1) Ask me to open the dispute now
   - I will re-run the eligibility check for the transaction and, if eligible, open the dispute on your behalf.
   - I’ll tell you the dispute reference and next steps immediately after.
   - I’ll also list the exact evidence we’re likely to need.

2) Try the merchant first
   - Contact the merchant and request shipment tracking, refund, or a resolution.
   - If the merchant won’t resolve it, come back here and I can open the dispute for you. Trying the merchant first is often faster.

3) Have me escalate to a human agent
   - I can escalate to a specialist to review the case or help contact the merchant. Tell me if you want me to escalate.

What happens after you pick
- If we open a dispute: case moves to under_review; you may receive a request for evidence (7‑day deadline). Possible outcomes: provisional credit, upheld, or declined.
- If you contact the merchant first and that fails: come back and I’ll open the dispute (with another eligibility check).

What I need from you now
- Tell me which option you want. If you want me to open the dispute, confirm which transaction to target (I will identify it if you prefer).

fragments.text:
Dispute handling process
## Evidence requirements
The customer may be asked for supporting evidence: an order confirmation, a
delivery record, correspondence with the merchant. Failure to supply requested
evidence within 7 calendar days results in the case being declined.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Case states
A dispute moves through: open, under_review, provisional_credit,
resolved_upheld, resolved_declined. Only open and under_review cases can be
withdrawn by the customer.
